protocol.name: treeland_output_manager_unstable_v2

protocol.description:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.
This protocol provides two capabilities to privileged clients such as display configuration panels:
1. Designating one connected output as the primary output, which the compositor may use to decide placement of panels, notifications, and newly opened windows.
2. Adjusting the color temperature and brightness of individual outputs via a double-buffered pending/commit model.
The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

interface.name: treeland_output_manager_v2

description.summary: primary output and picture control manager

interface.description:
A singleton global that exposes two capabilities: designating the primary output and creating per-output picture control objects.
Only one client should bind this interface at a time. The compositor may not advertise this global to additional clients, or may ignore requests from them, while a binding is already active.
On binding, the compositor immediately emits a primary_output event carrying the currently designated primary output, or null if no primary output has been designated.

enum.name: primary_output_error

description.summary: reasons a set_primary_output request was rejected

enum.description: Reasons returned by the primary_output_failed event.

entry.name: invalid_output
entry.summary: the provided output is null, disabled, or no longer available

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the treeland_output_manager_v2 object.
Existing treeland_output_picture_control_v2 objects created through this manager are not affected and must be destroyed separately by the client.

request.name: set_primary_output

description.summary: designate an output as the primary output

request.description:
Designate the given output as the primary output. The compositor uses the primary output as a hint for panel placement, initial window positioning, and other compositor-defined policies.
The output must be a currently enabled, available wl_output. If the output is disabled or no longer available, the compositor rejects the request and emits a primary_output_failed event; the primary output designation is unchanged.
The compositor applies a successful change immediately and confirms it by emitting a primary_output event carrying the newly designated primary output.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: an enabled output to designate as primary

request.name: get_picture_control

description.summary: create a picture control object for an output

request.description:
Create a treeland_output_picture_control_v2 object bound to the given output. The returned object allows the client to adjust the color temperature and brightness of that output.
For any live wl_output resource this request always succeeds without a protocol error, regardless of the output state — enabled, disabled, or no longer present in the configuration. An invalid or destroyed object id, or an object of another type, is still rejected by the core protocol (wl_display.invalid_object). If the bound output is later destroyed or not recognized by the compositor, subsequent commits fail with the invalid_output result.
Multiple picture control objects may exist for the same output at the same time; each object reports value changes independently.
If the output is disabled while a picture control object is bound to it, commits may fail; the compositor reports the outcome through the result event and leaves the applied settings unchanged.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: new picture control object for the given output

event.name: primary_output
event.description:
Emitted by the compositor to report the current primary output. This event is sent once immediately after the client binds this interface, and again whenever the primary output designation changes — whether in response to a set_primary_output request or through a compositor-driven fallback.
When the designated primary output is disconnected or disabled, the compositor automatically selects another available output as the new primary and emits this event with it. When no output is currently available, the event is emitted with a null output.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the currently designated primary output, or null when none is available

event.name: primary_output_failed
event.description: Emitted when a set_primary_output request cannot be applied, indicating that the primary output designation is unchanged. The error identifies why the request was rejected: the provided output was disabled or no longer available.

arg.name: error
arg.summary: why the set_primary_output request was rejected

interface.name: treeland_output_picture_control_v2

description.summary: per-output color temperature and brightness control

interface.description:
Represents a picture control session bound to a specific output, created by treeland_output_manager_v2.get_picture_control.
Color temperature and brightness are managed via a double-buffered pending/commit model. The client accumulates changes with set_color_temperature and set_brightness, then atomically applies them with a single commit request. After a successful commit the compositor emits a color_temperature or brightness event for each value that actually changed.
On creation, the compositor emits color_temperature and brightness events to report the current values of the output before the client has made any changes.
Clients should destroy this object when the associated wl_output is destroyed; otherwise subsequent commits fail with the invalid_output result.

enum.name: commit_result
enum.description: Indicates whether the preceding commit request was applied successfully, and if not, whether it failed because a pending value is outside its valid range, because the output does not support the requested adjustment, because the associated output is no longer available, or for another transient or unknown reason.

entry.name: success
entry.summary: all pending settings were applied successfully

entry.name: failed
entry.summary: the commit failed to apply for a transient or unknown reason; settings remain unchanged

entry.name: unsupported
entry.summary: the output does not support the requested adjustment, for example when its hardware cannot apply color temperature changes; settings remain unchanged

entry.name: invalid_output
entry.summary: the associated output is destroyed or not recognized; settings remain unchanged

entry.name: invalid_color_temperature
entry.summary: the pending color temperature is outside the valid range [1000, 20000]; settings remain unchanged

entry.name: invalid_brightness
entry.summary: the pending brightness is outside the valid range [0.0, 100.0]; settings remain unchanged

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the treeland_output_picture_control_v2 object and release all associated compositor resources. Any uncommitted pending settings are discarded.
After this request the compositor will no longer send result, color_temperature, or brightness events on this object.

request.name: set_color_temperature
request.description:
Set the pending color temperature for the output. The value is not applied until the client sends a commit request.
Valid range is [1000, 20000] Kelvin. A value outside this range is stored in the pending state but causes the next commit to fail with the invalid_color_temperature result.
Multiple calls before commit replace the pending value; only the last value is applied.

arg.name: temperature
arg.summary: color temperature in Kelvin, in the range [1000, 20000]

request.name: set_brightness
request.description:
Set the pending brightness for the output. The value is not applied until the client sends a commit request.
Valid range is [0.0, 100.0]. A value outside this range is stored in the pending state but causes the next commit to fail with the invalid_brightness result.
Multiple calls before commit replace the pending value; only the last value is applied.

request.name: commit
request.description:
Atomically apply all pending color temperature and brightness values accumulated since the last commit. The compositor always responds with a result event indicating success or failure. After a successful commit the compositor emits a color_temperature or brightness event for each value that actually changed.
It is valid to call commit without any preceding set_* requests; the compositor treats this as a no-op that succeeds without changing any value.
A failed commit reports its cause through the result event. The compositor checks the pending values first: a color temperature outside [1000, 20000] fails with invalid_color_temperature, and a brightness outside [0.0, 100.0] fails with invalid_brightness. The failure is otherwise caused by the output: it does not support the requested adjustment (unsupported, retrying the same settings is unlikely to succeed), it has been destroyed or is no longer recognized (invalid_output), or the commit could not be applied for a transient or unknown reason (failed). In every failure case the applied settings remain unchanged.

event.name: result

description.summary: result of the last commit request

event.description: Emitted by the compositor in response to every commit request, including commits with no pending changes, to indicate whether the settings were applied. Besides the failed, unsupported, and invalid_output causes, the invalid_color_temperature and invalid_brightness results indicate that a pending value is outside its valid range. After a successful commit, a color_temperature or brightness event is emitted for each value that actually changed.

arg.name: result
arg.summary: whether the commit succeeded or failed

event.name: color_temperature

description.summary: current color temperature of the output

event.description:
Reports the currently applied color temperature of the output. Emitted once immediately after the treeland_output_picture_control_v2 object is created to provide the initial value, and again whenever the applied color temperature changes — whether through a commit on this object, a commit on another color control object for the same output, or a compositor-driven change such as a system setting update.
Color temperature is expressed in Kelvin on a Planckian locus, in the range [1000, 20000].

event.name: brightness
event.description:
Reports the currently applied brightness of the output. Emitted once immediately after the treeland_output_picture_control_v2 object is created to provide the initial value, and again whenever the applied brightness changes — whether through a commit on this object, a commit on another picture control object for the same output, or a compositor-driven change such as a system setting update.
Brightness is expressed as a percentage in the range [0.0, 100.0].

arg.name: brightness
arg.summary: current brightness level in the range [0.0, 100.0]
